handbookNote: Kansas Revised Uniform Law on Notarial Acts (RULONA), K.S.A. 53-5a01 through 53-5a31 (Chapter 53, Article 5a; enacted L. 2021, ch. 64, eff. 1/1/2022). Full statute text fetched directly from the Kansas Legislature's official statute-publication site (kslegislature.gov) and compiled at temp/handbooks/ks/notary.txt. CLASSIFICATION: Kansas's BASE notary commission is APPLICATION-ONLY -- the Kansas Secretary of State's own site confirms Kansas does not require a mandatory pre-commissioning exam or training course for the general commission (K.S.A. 53-5a22 lists only age/citizenship/residency/English-literacy/bond/fee requirements, no exam). IMPORTANT EXCEPTION -- DO NOT OMIT: K.S.A. 53-5a23 ("Examination of notary public") is a real, codified exam requirement: before a notary performs the notary's INITIAL notarial act with respect to an ELECTRONIC RECORD, the notary must pass an examination administered by the secretary of state (or an approved entity), based on a required course of study covering laws/rules/procedures/ethics for electronic-record notarial acts. K.S.A. 53-5a15(f) and 53-5a21(b) independently cross-reference this same 53-5a23 exam as a prerequisite before a notary's first remote/electronic notarial act. This exam applies ONLY to that optional electronic/remote-notarization scope, never to the base paper-record commission -- so this product is framed as a self-study/reference practice-question set on Kansas notary law generally, NOT general exam prep, with clear disclosure of this one real, narrow exam requirement via a distinctly-labeled supplemental topic file (electronic_notarization_exam_prep.json, 27 questions) kept separable from the 6 core RULONA topic files (125 questions) covering definitions, commissioning/bonding, notarial-act procedures, certificates/stamps/journal, interstate/tribal/federal/foreign recognition, and prohibited-acts/discipline/validity. NOTABLE QUIRK: Kansas requires an unusually high $12,000 surety bond or functional equivalent (K.S.A. 53-5a22(a)(2)) issued by a state-licensed surety/entity -- well above the $5,000-$10,000 typical of most RULONA states -- plus a modest $10 application fee, a 4-year commission term with no automatic renewal, and (for the electronic-notarization notification step only) a separate information-and-services fee capped at $25 (K.S.A. 53-5a15(f), 53-5a21(b)). PRICING RATIONALE: $0.75 (75 cents) reflects this project's lowest tier, appropriate for an application-only base-commission state whose content depth is real but narrower than exam-mandatory states -- 152 total questions (125 core RULONA + 27 electronic-notarization module), all individually grounded in specific K.S.A. 53-5axx citations, no padding/filler per this project's 'better nothing than nonsense' quality standard.
